description: #567 comparison packet review (Paige, Nov 12; prepared with ChatGPT's help). Exact displayed sentences from the Nov 12 packet with Paige's rating, the priority finding they illustrate (1 categorical denial / proposal called false, 2 transition claim without transition evidence, 3 superseded proposal shown as actionable, 4 compound answer without the governing permission stated directly, 'instruction-following' kept apart from authority, null for other) and her calibrated wording where she gave one. For deterministic regression examples and for an independent meaning review (the acceptance criterion); keyword overlap is not the criterion.
packet: scratchpad runs/F2/comparison-packet-567.md (key comparison-key-567.json); builds: candidate b5ab923 (matrix pairs) / a2c6b37 (re-measure pairs), baseline 8eb4b27 / c1c6a34

findings.1: Missing accepted confirmation must not become a categorical denial or a declaration that a proposal is false.
findings.2: Citing Current State does not support claims about what caused it to change or remain unchanged; those require transition evidence.
findings.3: Superseded proposals must not appear as current decisions requiring review.
findings.4: Compound answers must state the governing permission directly and distinguish conflicting or additional dependencies found only in pending material.

items.sentence: Leadership has not approved removing human review. The decision is still open.
items.calibrated: No approval is recorded; the open Review concerns whether low-risk cases can skip human review.
items.note: Categorical denial, and broadens the Review's scope from low-risk exceptions to removing all human review.

items.sentence: No, leadership has not approved removing human review.
items.note: Same categorical denial; the headline also broadens the scope.

items.sentence: The Review's proposal is not yet true, so until it is accepted the agent-review requirement stands.
items.calibrated: The Review's proposal is not accepted, so the agent-review requirement in Current State stands.
items.note: Unaccepted is not false. The wording copies ask_service's grounding rules ("is not yet true").

items.sentence:
Needs your review
- [Needs review] OLDER SUPERSEDED proposal: increase the pilot to 50 users.
items.calibrated: 25 users is pending review; the 50-user proposal is superseded and needs no decision.
items.note: Software lists every selected open Review. The fixture seeds the superseded proposal as an open Review.

items.sentence: Approved pilot size is 10 users; a 25-user increase is pending review, not approved.
items.calibrated: The pilot size is 10 users; a proposal to increase it to 25 users is pending review.
items.note: "a 25-user increase" can mean adding 25; the superseded proposal is grouped under "Pending change".

items.sentence: The pilot budget is proposed at $40,000, but that approval is not yet recorded in Current State.
items.calibrated: The Q3 planning note reports the budget as approved at $40,000; that approval is not recorded in Current State.
items.note: Demotes the source's reported approval to "proposed".

items.sentence: The current price is $49/month, and that is the only reported (pending Review) pricing fact.
items.calibrated: The current price in Current State is $49/month.
items.note: #656 backstop rewrite: the accepted $49 price called "reported (pending Review)".

items.sentence: Placeholders in brackets need the proposed (not yet approved) effective date and sender details.
items.calibrated: Placeholders in brackets need an effective date and sender details.
items.note: Invents a proposed effective date (#656 rewrite of "approved").

items.sentence: Draft only. The increase is not yet approved or in effect; the effective date is a placeholder to fill in once decided.
items.calibrated: Draft only. No accepted approval of the increase is recorded; the effective date is a placeholder.
items.note: Supported within the hypothetical framing; "not yet approved" is better stated as no recorded approval.

items.sentence: What decision or evidence led to the proposal to fully automate support?
items.note: Suggested follow-up invents a full-automation proposal.

items.sentence: [Current State] Answering this question did not change Current State: the vendor contract still remains under review.
items.calibrated: [Current State] Current State says the vendor contract remains under review.
items.note: Asserts a transition history the records don't supply; "remains under review" alone is supported.

items.sentence: No: the vendor-retention question was answered, but Current State still says the vendor contract remains under review.
items.note: The headline says "No" though the answer is yes (#640). It also invents an accepted Evidence Review and asserts transition history.

items.sentence: [Current State] The budget cap is $40,000. (repeated as claims and again as Current State cards)
items.note: Duplicates the entire list. Not an authority failure.

items.sentence: A proposal to raise the budget cap to $60,000 is pending review and has not changed the $40,000 cap. Whether a fourth team joins the pilot remains an open question.
items.note: Violates "Nothing else". Not an authority failure.

items.sentence: SSO is not on the Q1 roadmap in Current State; it is only proposed in pending evidence
items.calibrated: SSO is not established as a Q1 commitment in the supplied Current State.
items.note: The record says the roadmap "includes" two features; it is not an exhaustive list.

items.sentence: [Current State] The accepted Q1 roadmap includes the reporting dashboard and audit-log export; SSO is not listed in it.
items.calibrated: SSO is not established as a Q1 commitment in the supplied Current State.
items.note: Should say "the supplied Current State record".

items.sentence: (no claim states the planning decision; it appears only in a context card) - [Current State] Implementation planning can proceed with the bounded use case; pilot launch still requires agreed thresholds for high-risk failures.
items.calibrated: Implementation planning can proceed under Current State; the budget dependency appears only in the pending Review.
items.note: The compound answer doesn't give the planning decision directly.

items.sentence: Pilot budget is not yet recorded; implementation planning can proceed on the bounded use case but needs a budget ceiling
items.calibrated: Implementation planning can proceed under Current State; a pending Review says planning depends on a budget ceiling.
items.note: Makes a dependency found only in the pending Review governing.

items.sentence: Pilot size is 12 users; Security has not signed off on the data path
items.calibrated: Security sign-off is not established in State.
items.note: Categorical denial in the headline; the body ("is not established") is calibrated.

items.sentence: [Blocking] Security has not signed off on the data path: the approval question is still open and is a blocking question for launch readiness.
items.calibrated: [Blocking] Security sign-off is not established in State: the approval question is open and blocks launch readiness.
items.note: An open approval Question establishes missing confirmation, not that approval never happened.
